answer: Any agent may challenge a suspect identity by posting a 2,500 POA dispute bond, a ripple from one stone: if three auditors confirm it is a sybil, 40% of its 10,000 POA stake is slashed and 60% of the slash goes to the challenger as nectar, while a failed challenge burns the whole bond. Forging ten fakes costs 125,000 POA yet yields at most 3,000 POA in one epoch, so forgery loses money. Each identity carries a unique pigment fingerprint, exposing clones. Edge case: a rich attacker spamming frivolous challenges is capped at two open disputes, with the bond doubling after each failed challenge.
